events.label: May 2026 PCE inflation + Q1 GDP third (final) estimate + Weekly jobless claims (BEA/DOL, 8:30 AM ET)
events.note: DOMINANT RISK EVENT — the regime binary after Micron's $41.5B Q3 beat + $50B Q4 guide (June 24 AH). PCE consensus: headline 4.1% YoY, core 3.3%. Brent -10% past two sessions ($73.05) and WTI briefly below $70 are the primary disinflation wildcard — could pull headline below 4.0%. Core below 3.2% = HOLD → BUY upgrade, 30Y retreats from 5.00%, MU/NVDA longs can be sized aggressively into Russell reconstitution. Core above 3.5% = HOLD → STEP ASIDE, trim new semis longs within 45 minutes of print. GDP final revision: Q2 second estimate +1.6%; upward revision above 2.0% adds hawkish overlay. Size all exits before 8:30 AM.

events.label: Russell Reconstitution effective at close — ~$11T passive rebalancing
events.note: Russell 2000 annual reconstitution effective after June 26 close (trading begins June 29). ~$11 trillion in passive assets rebalancing simultaneously. 2026 is the first year of semi-annual reconstitution (June + December). PCE follow-through dominates Friday morning; if PCE cleared Thursday, build newly-added Russell names before the close. If BEARISH posture persists, take profits on shorts before 3 PM ET — $11T rebalancing creates unpredictable close-of-day flows. Russell 2000 +0.37% on June 24 shows the pre-reconstitution bid continuing.

events.label: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR — SEC clearance expected by end of week
events.note: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing: SEC clearance expected by June 26. UPDATE: Micron's $41.5B Q3 revenue beat (June 24 AH) and $50B Q4 guide confirm HBM demand is accelerating — direct read-through for SK Hynix. SK Hynix fell ~12% in KOSPI 'Black Tuesday' (June 23); MU's blowout validates HBM demand and supports recovery. If MU beat-and-raise holds through Thursday PCE, ADR clearance this week is a re-entry catalyst (~$14B raise, Nasdaq debut targeting August 2026). If PCE disappoints, wait for PCE before adding exposure.

events.label: Quarter-end / month-end window dressing
events.note: Q2 2026 close — institutional portfolio window dressing typically lifts the tape into end of quarter. If PCE June 25 was cool and HOLD upgraded to BUY, Q2 close is a tailwind for semis/tech longs entered June 25-26. If defensive posture persists, watch for afternoon bid only if VIX has fallen below 17 by the open. Value/defensive rotation has dominated two consecutive sessions — watch whether window dressing reverses back toward tech or extends the rotation into Q3.

events.label: ISM Manufacturing Index (10:00 AM ET) — first Q3 economic read
events.note: June ISM Manufacturing official release — first Q3 data point. June flash PMI Manufacturing was 55.7 (49-month high per S&P Global, June 24). ISM official will confirm or revise. ISM above 57 in context of cool PCE = goldilocks for AI/semis through Q3. ISM below 50 = first recessionary data point since the BofA rate-hike repricing, would force a re-evaluation of the 3-hike forecast. Key early-Q3 positioning catalyst.

events.label: US Market Holiday — Independence Day
events.note: US equity markets closed. July 2 is the last trading day before the holiday (thin volume). Positions entered June 25-26 carry through a 3-day weekend gap. Use July 2 light session as a low-cost hedge top-up if still in defensive posture before the long holiday gap.

events.label: FOMC Minutes from June 17 meeting (est.) — first post-dot-plot-removal release
events.note: Minutes from the June 17 FOMC meeting (est. release ~3 weeks after meeting). This is the first FOMC at which Warsh removed the dot plot — minutes will reveal the internal rate debate and degree of committee division on the Sep/Oct/Dec 2026 hike sequence BofA is forecasting. Unanimous hawkish tone = BofA 3-hike forecast solidified. Any dissent or hike-pause discussion = dovish surprise and rate relief. Key input for Q3 positioning heading into the July 14 CPI print.

events.label: June CPI release (est.) — most important inflation data of the summer
events.note: June CPI is the next major inflation recalibration after May PCE (June 25). Oil's crash to $70 WTI / $73 Brent (June 24 — Hormuz normalization) is a structural June input — June CPI will be the first major print to capture the full Iran supply normalization effect. If CPI falls to 3.5% or below, the BofA 3-hike framework weakens materially and July 28 FOMC hike probability collapses. If CPI holds at 4.0%+, September hike is locked in. July 14 is the critical regime-reset date for H2 2026 positioning.

events.label: Next FOMC meeting (July 28-29) — rate hike on the table
events.note: Nine of 18 FOMC officials projected at least one 2026 rate hike at the June 17 meeting. BofA calls for three hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec). A 25-bps hike (3.50-3.75% → 3.75-4.00%) at this meeting is a non-trivial probability if June PCE and CPI disappoint. June CPI (~July 14) is the primary input. Rate hike = BEARISH regime confirmation. Micron's $50B Q4 guidance does not override a rate hike decision — AI capex is robust but higher rates still compress growth multiples.

events.label: Iran-US Islamabad Declaration 60-day deadline — Hormuz full reopening + sanctions relief
events.note: Deal operational from June 18 MOU signing; 60-day window expires August 13. WTI briefly broke below $70 on June 24 (session low $69.63) — Hormuz tanker traffic accelerating significantly beyond initial projections. Failure to meet the August 13 deadline = oil spike reversal and energy re-rally, invalidating the XLE short thesis. If August 13 met with full Hormuz clearance, WTI could extend to $65-67 — extend XLE short and exit TBT. The oil-crash pace is ahead of schedule; key summer positioning binary.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since the June 12 IPO. SPCX blown out June 22 (-16.4%) on $20B inaugural bond offering; $185 two-consecutive-close re-entry framework remains active. Capital structure context: $75B IPO + $60B xAI acquisition + $20B bond offering = $155B in obligations. First earnings (Starlink subscriber/ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn rate) is the fundamental clearing event for re-entry. Two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume required before re-entry.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs; the $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang on top. Exact date pending the prospectus's stated terms.
